title: Social Proof: Truths Are Us
coreMove: Ask whether the crowd signal is real, relevant, and made of people comparable to you.
sourcePressure: The source centers popularity cues, uncertainty, similarity, pluralistic ignorance, staged audience reactions, engineered popularity, norm messages that can backfire, and the defense of checking the social signal.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not make this a blanket warning against crowds; the lesson is how uncertainty borrows certainty from visible behavior.

exampleSpecs.domain: trailhead safety board before a flooded creek crossing
exampleSpecs.audience: a hiker watching three groups continue down the path
exampleSpecs.stakes: following visible confidence into unsafe water
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the hiker checks whether the groups ahead match her gear and route before treating their movement as evidence
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a damp trail map curling under a plexiglass cover

exampleSpecs.domain: auction preview for used restaurant equipment
exampleSpecs.audience: a first-time cafe owner bidding on an espresso machine
exampleSpecs.stakes: overbidding because a ring of bidders gathers near one machine
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner asks the auctioneer whether the crowd is watching the machine or waiting for the lot beside it
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stainless-steel portafilter tagged with a yellow lot number

exampleSpecs.domain: apartment building lobby during a smoke alarm chirp
exampleSpecs.audience: a tenant deciding whether to call emergency services
exampleSpecs.stakes: pluralistic ignorance while everyone watches everyone else
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the tenant sees neighbors standing still, names the uncertainty out loud, and assigns one person to check the stairwell while another calls
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a smoke alarm light blinking above the mailboxes

exampleSpecs.audience: an adult learner choosing a course level
exampleSpecs.stakes: selecting the popular beginner track despite already knowing the material
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the learner notices the thousands enrolled badge and takes the placement quiz instead of copying the majority
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a green progress owl beside a course list

exampleSpecs.audience: a grower reading a sign about common dumping behavior
exampleSpecs.stakes: a descriptive norm sign accidentally making dumping seem normal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the grower revises the sign from many people dumped last year to nine out of ten brought containers here
exampleSpecs.firstImage: empty chemical jugs stacked in a wire crate

exampleSpecs.audience: a director interpreting laughter in the room
exampleSpecs.stakes: mistaking planted audience reaction for real response
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director compares laugh timing between invited friends in the front row and strangers in the back rows
exampleSpecs.firstImage: paper feedback cards on a red velvet seat

skillTargets: identify uncertainty as the opening for social proof
test whether visible behavior comes from comparable others
recognize pluralistic ignorance in group silence
revise norm messages that accidentally endorse bad behavior

tryThisNowSpec: When you see a popularity label today, ask one exact question: popular with whom, and were they deciding under the same conditions as me?
